commands.cmd: fresh offline tarball consumer install plus installed mixed TSRX/TSX write and check smoke test

summary: Delivered the installable non-fork formatter fallback: standard files delegate directly to official Oxfmt 0.57.0/0.59.0, TSRX uses a lazy swappable backend, the shared JSONC config subset is validated, editor calls are no-write, mixed batches stage TSRX failures, and explicit backend instability is rejected after three passes. The retained first red run had 0/7 passing before the package/CLI/aliases existed; a later custom-backend regression failed 4/5 before the convergence contract was fixed. Final tests pass 22/22. A fresh offline tarball consumer formatted and then checked a mixed TSRX/TSX batch. On an Apple M5 Pro, small TSRX averaged 0.71 ms, standard TSX p95 was 1.019x direct Oxfmt, and 178 valid read-only Markless files formatted at 2.28 MiB/s with zero second-call failures or differences.
deviations: The published fallback is @tsrx/prettier-plugin 0.3.97 on Prettier 3.9.5, not native Oxfmt. It clears the interim >=2.0 MiB/s floor but not the final >=15 MiB/s native formatter gate; T008 retains that required work explicitly.
The published printer cannot serialize one valid BigInt Markless fixture. The failure is retained, reported, and byte-for-byte no-write rather than misrepresented as supported.
Twelve additional Markless files are intentionally incomplete or error-oriented editor/protocol fixtures and are reported outside the 178-file valid intersection; no external file was changed.
